title: Action record schema: OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions + tamper-evident log
outcome: A draft per-action record schema mapped to OTel GenAI attributes, with the gaps (state read/write sets) and a tamper-evidence mechanism chosen
acceptance: ≥5 primary sources with URLs, including the official OTel GenAI semconv spec (with version/stability status) and RFC 9162 or Sigstore Rekor/Trillian docs
Field table: proposed action-record field × OTel attribute if one exists (or 'gap') × why TTI/TTC/recovery needs it
Comparison of ≥3 tamper-evidence options (hash chain, Merkle log, transparency log) on guarantees, verification cost, prototype effort
'Implications for our design' section for Recorder and Monitor
summary:
OTel GenAI conventions (agent/tool spans, gen_ai.agent.id, tool.call.*, conversation.id) cover who called what, but have NO state read/write, effect-class, delegation or causal-edge fields: those are our gap fields (ks.*). All gen_ai.* still Development; spec moved to semantic-conventions-genai repo in Jun 2026 (no release found); execute_tool span details unverified (repo docs not fetchable).
Tamper-evidence: chose per-agent hash chain inside an RFC 9162-style Merkle log with Ed25519 signed checkpoints published outside agents' reach; hash chain alone fails against full rewrite; Rekor/Trillian too heavy for prototype.
Report has 19-field draft record, 3-option comparison, Recorder and Monitor implications.
Top design implication: the gateway (not the agent) writes records including read_set/write_set/caused_by, since these enable selective rollback and blast-radius at detection time.
